chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all of them said:
We presented the Book of Inheritance from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he said: 'It is authentic.'
And among what was in it was that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) set the blood money (diyah) of the fetus at one hundred dinars.
When another creation is formed in it, which is the soul, then at that time it is a complete life (nafs) with a full blood money of one thousand dinars, whether it is male or female.

And if the woman is killed while she is in a complete pregnancy, and her child has not fallen out, and it is not known whether it is male or female, and it is not known whether it died after her or before her, then its blood money is two halves: half the blood money of the male and half the blood money of the female.
And the blood money of the woman is complete after that.
And we have included detailed narrations regarding the details of the fetus's blood money in our Great Book; whoever wishes to see them may refer to it from there.

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for death/injury

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a fetus in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain in al-Istibsar establishes the jurisprudential basis for fetal blood money (diyah), distinguishing between the pre-soul stage (100 dinars) and post-soul stage (1,000 dinars for males, 500 for females). It further addresses the legal complexity of indeterminate cases where a pregnant woman is killed, prescribing a split compensation of half the male and half the female rates to account for uncertainty in gender and timing of death.
